For 1 Respondent : Mr.S.Vinoth Kumar  Government Advocat  ORDER
This Criminal Original Petition has been filed by the petitioner to quash the case in C.C.No.206 of 2025 pending before the XIII Metropolitan Magistrate, Egmore.
2. The case of the prosecution as per the defacto complainant is that he had entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with the petitioner for construction of his house.
Subsequently, the defacto complainant had started to construct the house and he had also spent Rs.46,26,927/- out of which, the petitioner had paid a sum of Rs.27,80,000/- on various instalments.

When the construction was in the midway, the defacto complainant approached the petitioner for money for further construction for which, the petitioner refused to give the same and also stated that he would carry on further construction by https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 26/06/2025 08:34:28 pm ) engaging some other persons.
Hence, the defacto complainant asked the petitioner to pay the balance amount of Rs.18,46,927/- which he had spent.
However, the petitioner evaded to pay the balance amount and cheated the defacto complainant.

Hence, based on the complaint given by the defacto complainant, the case in FIR No. 81 of 2024 was registered by the first respondent police against the petitioner for the offence under Sections 406 and 420 IPC and after completion of investigation, the respondent police filed the charge sheet and the same was taken on file in C.C.No.206 of 2025 on the file of the XIII Metropolitan Magistrate, Egmore.

Pending case, the petitioner has filed the present petition to quash the C.C.
3.

Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Advocate (Crl. Side)
appearing for the first respondent police and also perused the materials available on record.
4. It is seen from the records that there is a construction agreement dated 07.05.2023 between the defacto complainant and the mother of the petitioner.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

When the construction was in the mid way, there was a dispute between the contractor and the building owner and therefore, the contractor/defacto complainant has lodged complaint against the petitioner.
5. Further, a reading of the agreement, the complaint and the allegations against the petitioner shows that there is a dispute of breach of contract which is purely civil in nature.
According to the petitioner, the defacto complainant had done faulty construction and also used substandard quality materials which requires technical expert opinion.
The Department of Police has no role to play with the same and hence, registering FIR is nothing but abuse of process of law.
6. Therefore, the case in C.C.No.206 of 2025 pending on the file of the XIII Metropolitan Magistrate, Egmore is quashed.
7. However, the defacto complainant is at liberty to work out his remedy before the competent authority.
